source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine Fuel - Air Cleaners, p.6M-14

procedures.title: Thermostatically controlled air cleaner: inspect and test
procedures.applies_to: all models (where thermostatic air cleaner fitted)
steps: Apply at least 9 inches of vacuum (engine or separate source) to the vacuum motor fitting.
The damper should close the cold air passage and open the hot air pipe for as long as vacuum is applied.
If the motor will not move the damper under direct vacuum, check that its linkage is connected to the door and not binding.
If the linkage is fine, replace the motor; if the motor passes, replace the sensor.

procedures.title: Air cleaner vacuum motor: replace
procedures.applies_to: all models (where thermostatic air cleaner fitted)
steps: Remove the air cleaner from the engine.
Drill out the spot welds holding the motor strap to the snorkel tube.
Lift the motor and unhook its linkage rod from the damper door.
Replacement: drill a 7/64" hole in the snorkel tube at the center of the strap location (see figure 7A in the manual).
Hook the motor linkage to the damper door and fasten the strap with a sheet metal screw.
Refit the air cleaner and check motor and damper operation.

procedures.title: Air cleaner temperature sensor: replace
procedures.applies_to: all models (where thermostatic air cleaner fitted)
steps: Remove the air cleaner and disconnect the vacuum hoses at the sensor.
Pry up the retaining clip tabs, noting the sensor's position so the new one goes in the same way.
Fit the new sensor and gasket in the noted position.
Press the clip on, supporting the sensor by its sides so the center mechanism is not damaged.
Refit the air cleaner and reconnect the vacuum hoses.
